title: Why You Should Eat Lunch With Your Students https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2013/10/12/why-you-should-eat-lunch-with-your-students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin recommends occasionally—once or twice a month—eating lunch with students in their own space, while preserving most lunch breaks as personal time. He argues this informal, agenda-free presence builds rapport more effortlessly than forced attempts at friendliness, and it proves to students, especially the most challenging ones, that misbehavior earlier in the day carries no lingering resentment. He also highlights the social benefit for shy or less popular students, who benefit from watching a teacher model easy, inclusive conversation. He is careful to distinguish this practice from using lunch as a transactional reward for good behavior, which he says undermines authentic rapport entirely.
points: Eating lunch with students should be occasional (once or twice a month), not routine, preserving most lunch periods as personal teacher time.
Showing up without an agenda demonstrates concretely that 'every day is a new day' and that earlier misbehavior carries no lingering resentment.
The practice is especially valuable for building trust with the most challenging students, who need extra convincing that grace is unconditional.
Informal lunchtime presence benefits shy or socially awkward students by modeling inclusive, easy conversation they can observe and later emulate.
Using lunch as a reward for good behavior undermines authentic rapport and should not be confused with this unconditional practice.
quotes: But occasionally, maybe once or twice a month, it pays to eat lunch with your students. It pays to go where they go, to sit down in the lunch room right smack dab in their midst.
It proves to your class that, despite your faithful adherence to your classroom management plan, there are never any hard feelings.
Sound classroom management goes a long way toward creating an atmosphere of acceptance, edification, and social safety.
It’s important to note that buying your students lunch as a reward for good behavior doesn’t count and won’t in any way improve your relationships
It’s in your relationships, after all, where the lasting memories of your career are made.
